posts.text: Blir spennende med pre-silent newsletter i morgen.  Tenker at en samlet positiv oppdatering vil potensielt påvirke kursen mye mer enn sammenlignet med en nøytral-negativ oppdatering da det allerede er bakt inn mye skepsis ref. shortere og enkelte meglerhus.  Kanskje vi får mer informasjon og guiding i.f.m. Dealer Hub? ( en felles nordisk B2B-plattform som ble lansert av Vend i år.  Vært lite publisitet rundt dette synes jeg. Plattformen samler verktøy for profesjonelle bilforhandlere på tvers av deres nordiske markedsplasser: FINN (Norge), Blocket (Sverige), samt Bilbasen og DBA (Danmark).   Finansielt ligger Dealer Hub under Vends Mobility-vertikal. Selskapet har i 2026 opplevd noe flate inntekter, men har hatt lovende EBITDA-vekst (opp 16 % i Q2 2026) som følge av knallhard kostnadsdisiplin og forenkling av organisasjonen.   Short skvis og boost i kursen ? Her er hva AI sier hvis det blir positive oppdateringer:   A positive Q3 pre-silent newsletter could significantly impact short-selling activity on the Oslo Børs, potentially forcing a "short squeeze" or rapid position adjustments.  Because this newsletter format was explicitly introduced in 2025 following a regulatory overhaul by Finanstilsynet, it serves as the market's single most critical data check ahead of the silent period.  If the letter reveals unexpectedly strong volume numbers, it will disrupt short positions in several distinct ways:  ⚡ Mechanics of the Short-Seller Impact  - The Trigger for a Short Squeeze: If July–August listing volumes (particularly in macro-sensitive sectors like Jobs or Real Estate) turn sharply positive, algorithms will immediately push the stock upward at the 09:00 CEST opening bell. To cap their losses, short sellers will be forced to buy back shares on the open market, adding aggressive upward momentum to the stock price.  -Neutralizing the "Flat Revenue" Thesis: Bearish funds are primarily shorting Vend Marketplaces under the assumption that Nordic macroeconomic cooling is capping organic volume growth. Positive volume numbers directly invalidate this thesis, forcing structural shorts to reconsider their risk profile ahead of the October 27 earnings report.  -Collision with the Corporate Buyback Floor: Vend's highly active NOK 2 billion share buyback program is already purchasing shares daily to support the stock on the Oslo Børs. If short sellers are simultaneously forced to cover their positions alongside corporate brokers buying up available float, the lack of selling liquidity can accelerate the price jump.  What to look for at 07:00 CEST:   When reviewing the Mobility data in tomorrow's newsletter, look specifically for professional dealer volume growth. If professional listings are up year-over-year, it signals that corporate automotive spending is holding strong—a data point that will almost certainly force short sellers tracking the sector to hedge their positions.
